title: Strawberry Jam
subtitle: Classic soft-set strawberry jam for toast, scones, and sponges
excerpt: A straight British strawberry jam, whole fruit, granulated sugar, a squeeze of lemon. Makes about three 450 g jars. The lemon provides the acid the fruit needs to set.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton (1861), Pam Corbin in Preserves, and the NCHFP Home Canning guides all give the same 1:1 fruit-to-sugar ratio for strawberry jam.

recipe.batchNotes: Scale up to 2 kg of fruit at most — larger quantities take too long to reach setting point and the colour dulls.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Sterilise jars the day before to save time.

glossaryTerms.definition: The temperature at which jam will set when cooled, typically 104–105 °C. Confirmed by the wrinkle test: a spoonful on a chilled plate pushed with a fingertip should wrinkle rather than run.
To spoon off the foam that rises to the surface of jam during cooking. It is mostly air bubbles and won't affect the flavour, but removing it gives a clearer jar.

content.text: Strawberry jam is a short-fruit jam,  the fruit has low natural pectin, so it needs lemon juice to pull a set. The result is a soft, glossy, deeply fruited preserve that holds its colour well. It keeps 12 months unopened in a cool, dark cupboard.
Macerate the fruit in sugar overnight before cooking. This firms the berries so they hold their shape in the jar. Use the widest, heaviest pan you have, and have your jars hot when you fill them.

You need a wide, heavy-based jam pan (or the largest saucepan you own),  the wider the better, as surface area drives evaporation. Three sterilised 450 g jars with lids. A sugar thermometer is useful but the wrinkle test works just as well.

Layer the strawberries and sugar in the jam pan with the lemon juice. Cover and leave at room temperature for at least 4 hours, or overnight. The sugar draws juice from the fruit and begins to dissolve. This step is not optional,  it helps the berries hold their shape in the finished jam.

Wash the jars and lids in hot soapy water, rinse well, then place upright on a baking tray and put in the oven at 120 °C for 20 minutes. Leave them in the warm oven until you are ready to fill. Hot jam into hot jars prevents the glass cracking and stops condensation forming.
Put a small plate in the freezer. Set the pan over medium heat and stir until the sugar dissolves. Raise the heat to a rapid boil and stop stirring. Cook for 10 to 15 minutes. At 104 to 105 °C (the

), take the pan off the heat. Drop a teaspoon onto the chilled plate, leave a minute, then push it with your fingertip. If it wrinkles, the jam will set. If it runs, return to the boil for 2 to 3 minutes and test again.

any foam from the surface with a large spoon. Rest the jam for 10 minutes off the heat,  this helps the fruit stay suspended rather than floating to the top of the jar. Ladle into the hot jars, filling to within 5 mm of the rim. Seal immediately with the lids. The jam will thicken as it cools.

items.cause: Not enough pectin, or the boil was too short / too low to reach 104 °C.
items.fix: Return to the pan, add the juice of half a lemon, bring back to a rapid boil and test every 3 minutes. Most strawberry jams need 12 to 18 minutes of hard boil total.

items.symptom: Fruit floats to the top of the jar
items.cause: Jam was poured too hot, before the fruit had a chance to distribute evenly.
items.fix: Resting 10 minutes off the heat before jarring usually solves this. For next time, give the pan a gentle stir before ladling to redistribute the fruit.

items.symptom: Jam is too dark or tastes burnt
items.cause: The pan was too narrow, causing a long, slow cook at high heat.
items.fix: Use the widest pan available next time. A higher surface-to-volume ratio means faster evaporation at lower heat.

items.cause: Jars were not fully sterilised, or jam was jarred when cool, trapping condensation.
items.fix: Discard the affected jar. Always jar at 80 °C or above, into pre-warmed sterile jars, and seal immediately.

content.text: Sealed jars keep in a cool, dark cupboard for 12 months. Once opened, refrigerate and use within 4 weeks.
